corrected_draft.title: VA spokesperson denies DOGE access to veterans’ personal data
corrected_draft.description_short: A VA spokesperson said DOGE had not accessed Veterans’ or beneficiaries’ personal data, NPR reported on March 11, 2025.
corrected_draft.description_medium: NPR reported that a VA spokesperson said DOGE “does not have and has not had access” to Veterans’ or VA beneficiaries’ data. The article also quoted a DOGE spokesperson describing limited read-only access elsewhere in government. It documented denials and concerns, not a VA medical-record breach.
corrected_draft.description_long: In an NPR report published March 11, 2025, a VA spokesperson said DOGE “does not have and has not had access to Veterans’ or VA beneficiaries’ data.” The report discussed broader concerns about government agencies’ access to highly personal information. It separately quoted a DOGE spokesperson saying staff had read-only access to some data and that none of the information they could access contained personal health information of Medicare or Medicaid enrollees. VA Secretary Doug Collins had earlier addressed media concerns about benefits in an official February message, saying DOGE representatives at VA were reviewing contracts and that he was happy to partner with them. Collins also said Veterans’ benefits were not being cut and that the Veterans Benefits Administration was clearing cases faster. The statements document agency assurances and public concerns about access to sensitive data. NPR reported the spokesperson’s denial but did not publish a technical audit of VA systems or independently verify access logs.
